pairs.distinction: Learning is wanting to learn something for myself and not knowing how to begin; Skills is the world or my job now asking for skills I don't have.
pairs.reason: Wanting to pick up guitar and falling behind at work feel nothing alike, so a person knows which one is theirs.

pairs.distinction: Learning is about starting on a subject or skill; Direction is about a bigger goal in life and the steps to reach it.
pairs.reason: Someone who wants to learn Spanish and someone who wants a different life would each pick their own line without hesitating.

pairs.distinction: Direction is not knowing the steps toward a goal; Skills is knowing what's needed and not being able to do it yet.
pairs.reason: Missing a map and missing the ability are different gaps, and the fixes for each are different.

pairs.distinction: Stuck is feeling that life isn't moving at all, often without a clear goal; Direction is having a goal and no route to it.
pairs.reason: The line for Direction starts with knowing what I want, which someone who feels stuck usually can't say, so the choice is easy.

pairs.distinction: Lost myself is not knowing what I like or want any more; Stuck is knowing my life isn't moving forward.
pairs.reason: One is about who I am and the other is about where my life is going, and the alternative line for Lost myself makes that plain.

pairs.distinction: Lost myself is not knowing myself any more; Self-esteem is judging myself harshly.
pairs.reason: Someone who has lost track of what they want isn't necessarily hard on themselves, and the reverse is true too.

pairs.distinction: Procrastination is not starting the things I mean to do; Focus is my mind wandering once I've started.
pairs.reason: People can tell putting something off from drifting away from it partway through.

pairs.distinction: Career is being in the wrong line of work; Direction is knowing what I want, in work or anywhere else, and not how to get there.
pairs.reason: Someone in the wrong job may not yet know what they want instead, while Direction starts from a goal already in mind.

pairs.distinction: Career is about the job; Stuck is about life as a whole not moving.
pairs.reason: A person who likes their work can still feel their life is going nowhere, so the two don't collapse into one.

pairs.distinction: Creativity is missing making things; Fun is missing play and lightness of any kind.
pairs.reason: Someone who misses painting and someone who never gets to relax and play would each recognize only their own line.

pairs.distinction: Creativity is no longer making things of my own; Meaning is feeling my paid work doesn't matter.
pairs.reason: One is about time to create and the other is about whether a job is worth doing, and people know which they mean.
